source: Nair et al. (2024) Creative Problem Solving in Large Language and Vision Models
finding: Position paper. It links LLM search (tree search, MCTS, beam search over outputs) to Boden's exploratory creativity. It has no experiments.
numbers: No measured results. Only a conceptual mapping.
limits: The anchor paper for this subfield is a position paper, so it gives no effect sizes. All numbers below come from other studies.
agent_relevance: S3 search control has no direct empirical support from this paper; use the studies below.

source: Franceschelli and Musolesi (2025) On the Creativity of Large Language Models
finding: Argues trained models can at most show combinational or exploratory creativity, since they learn the training distribution. Calls for research on search-style generation.
numbers: No experiments.
limits: Theory only. Claim about transformational limits is untested.
agent_relevance: Do not assume the agent can leave its space by search alone; reframing needs an outside trigger.

source: Franceschelli (2026) On the Creativity of AI Agents
finding: Says LLM agents show interpolation and extrapolation (combinational, exploratory) but not hyperpolation (transformational). Notes no good test for it exists yet.
numbers: No experiments.
limits: Argument paper. Hyperpolation is hard to operationalise.
agent_relevance: Treat transformational creativity as unmeasured, not as proven impossible.

source: Yao et al. (2023) Tree of Thoughts
finding: Search over partial thoughts with model-scored states beats left-to-right decoding on Game of 24.
numbers: Game of 24 success: IO 7.3%, CoT 4.0%, CoT-SC(k=100) 9.0%, IO best of 100 33%, CoT best of 100 49%, ToT b=1 45%, ToT b=5 74% (GPT-4, 100 tasks).
limits: Task has a checkable goal and a short horizon. Evaluator is the same model. Costs more tokens.
agent_relevance: Strong support for S3: a small beam with a state check beats 100 blind samples. Best-of-100 CoT still lost to ToT (49% vs 74%).

source: Yao et al. (2023) Tree of Thoughts
finding: On open-ended Creative Writing, search gives a smaller, noisier gain, and the gain depends on a model-judged score.
numbers: Coherence (GPT-4 score 1-10): IO 6.19, CoT 6.93, ToT 7.56. Humans preferred ToT over CoT in 41 of 100 pairs, CoT over ToT in 21, 38 similar. Iterative refine lifted IO to 7.67 and ToT to 7.91.
limits: Metric is coherence, not novelty. Judge is a model. Simple refinement matched ToT, so search is not clearly needed here.
agent_relevance: In open mode, search buys coherence more than novelty. Do not read it as a creativity result.

source: Yao et al. (2023) Tree of Thoughts
finding: Backtracking matters: removing it hurts mini crosswords.
numbers: Word-level success: IO/CoT under 16%, ToT 60%, 4 of 20 games solved; without backtracking about 20%.
limits: 20 games only.
agent_relevance: Supports allowing return to earlier states in S3 when a check fails.

source: Wang et al. (2026) CreativeBench
finding: Benchmark of exploratory and combinational creativity in code with executable checks. Creativity = quality x novelty. Scaling helps combination but gives diminishing returns for exploration.
numbers: Best models pass under 60% of items; Gemini-2.5-Pro pass 53.8% (Combo) and 48.2% (Explore). Human check of 300 items: 89.1% valid.
limits: Code domain only. Novelty is an embedding/n-gram distance. The product metric mixes correctness and novelty.
agent_relevance: Exploration is not fixed by a bigger model; search control has to supply it.

source: Wang et al. (2026) CreativeBench
finding: Convergence-by-scaling: larger models become more correct but less divergent. Novelty falls or stays flat as size grows.
numbers: Normalised creativity rises with size only because Pass@1 rises; novelty declines or plateaus (Figure 4).
limits: Observed within the tested model families only.
agent_relevance: Matches our NoveltyBench finding. A strong model will not be more varied by default; diversity must be forced by code.

source: Wang et al. (2026) CreativeBench
finding: Reasoning mode helps constrained exploration more than combination.
numbers: Direction reported in Figure 5; the paper states reasoning mainly benefits constraint-driven exploration.
limits: I did not extract the per-model numbers.
agent_relevance: Constraints (forbid the usual method) plus reasoning are a cheap way to push search off the default path.

source: Wang et al. (2026) CreativeBench
finding: Evolutionary search (AlphaEvolve-style, GEPA) raises pass and creativity a little; a steering vector (EvoRePE) adds a further small gain.
numbers: Qwen2.5-7B Combo: vanilla creativity 0.168, +EvoRePE 0.174, AlphaEvolve 0.175, AlphaEvolve+EvoRePE 0.193. Pass@1 9.21% to 11.48%. Explore pass 4.11% to 5.75%. 10 seeds; EvoRePE Combo pass +0.80pp (CI 0.68-0.92).
limits: Gains are small in absolute terms. EvoRePE needs open weights, so it cannot be used on an API model.
agent_relevance: Evolutionary prompt search gives small, real gains; steering vectors are out of reach for a scaffold.

source: Bhushan et al. (2026) Can LLM Agents Discover?
finding: Agents' novelty relative to their own past (P-Creativity) falls over a run: they move from exploring to exploiting, in every setup tested.
numbers: 10 MLE-Bench tasks, AIDE and AIRA-Dojo. LLM judge vs human: Spearman 0.732 (GPT-5 judge). P-Creativity declines universally; agents converge faster than humans.
limits: 10 tasks. Judge validated on a human subset only.
agent_relevance: Search decays toward exploitation by itself. A scaffold needs a code-side rule that re-opens exploration.

source: Bhushan et al. (2026) Can LLM Agents Discover?
finding: Novelty and gain are decoupled. Agents reach regions more novel than gold-medal humans but do not turn that into performance.
numbers: Gold human H-creativity 0.744 (silver 0.524, bronze 0.293); GPT-5 AIDE 1.423 (p<1e-15). Medal rate: 21.25% of GPT-5 runs, 10.85% of Qwen3-32B runs. Correlation of change in impact vs change in P-creativity: human -0.111 (p<0.05), AIDE GPT-5 -0.021, AIDE Qwen3 0.056, AIRA Qwen3 -0.026.
limits: Medal rate is low for other reasons too (weak agent scaffolds).
agent_relevance: Novelty alone is not a target. Selection needs an outside check, as in G3 and G5.

source: Bhushan et al. (2026) Can LLM Agents Discover?
finding: After reaching a very novel state, agents mostly refine it and lose the novelty without gaining impact.
numbers: 92 episodes (top 20% H-creativity, bottom 20% impact): 87.0% led to refinement; 53.8% of refined episodes lost H-creativity next step; median impact change 0.000.
limits: Small subsample.
agent_relevance: Refining a novel idea does not reliably keep it novel. Branch, do not overwrite.

source: Bhushan et al. (2026) Can LLM Agents Discover?
finding: Search strategy changes the pattern. Greedy starts most novel and declines steeply; MCTS and evolutionary search keep lower but steadier novelty. Greedy also had the highest impact.
numbers: AIRA-Dojo, Qwen3-32B, 3 tasks (Figure 3). No effect sizes.
limits: 3 tasks, one model.
agent_relevance: Steadier novelty did not mean higher score; tune breadth to the task.

source: Si, Yang, Hashimoto (2024) Can LLMs Generate Novel Research Ideas?
finding: In a blind review by 79 experts, LLM-generated research ideas were rated more novel than 49 human expert ideas, and slightly weaker on feasibility.
numbers: Novelty 4.84 (human), 5.64 (AI), 5.81 (AI + human rerank); AI vs human p<0.05 (Welch t-tests, multiple-test corrected). Feasibility difference not significant (-0.29, p=0.36).
limits: Review of ideas, not outcomes. Reviewers agree weakly (56.1% split-half; NeurIPS 2021 was 66.0%).
agent_relevance: Search plus rerank gives novel ideas. Ratings are noisy, so do not trust one judge.

source: Si, Yang, Hashimoto (2024) Can LLMs Generate Novel Research Ideas?
finding: Over-generation hits a ceiling: repeated sampling mostly yields duplicates.
numbers: Cosine similarity above 0.8 counted as duplicate. Out of 4000 seed ideas per topic only about 200 were non-duplicate (about 5%). New-batch non-duplicate rate kept falling; accumulated unique ideas plateaued.
limits: One agent pipeline, 7 NLP topics.
agent_relevance: Samples from one model are not independent (G4). More samples without a dedupe or archive wastes budget.

source: Si, Yang, Hashimoto (2024) Can LLMs Generate Novel Research Ideas?
finding: LLM self-ranking is weak. Best zero-shot ranker beat chance only modestly; prompting tricks did not help.
numbers: Accept/reject pair task: Claude-3.5-Sonnet 71.4%, Claude-3-Opus 63.5%, GPT-4o 61.1%. No significant gain from few-shot or CoT.
limits: Proxy task from ICLR data.
agent_relevance: Supports G5: use a model ranker only as a weak filter.

source: Si, Hashimoto, Yang (2025) The Ideation-Execution Gap
finding: When 43 experts actually ran the ideas, AI ideas lost their novelty edge. Idea-stage novelty does not predict outcomes.
numbers: Drops after execution (1-10 scale): AI novelty -1.049, excitement -1.760, effectiveness -1.879; human ideas about -0.010, +0.078, -0.052. Gap difference FDR p=0.025 (novelty) to 0.001 (excitement). Rankings flipped on all metrics (e.g. excitement 3.90 AI vs 4.48 human), not significant.
limits: 43 projects. The execution flip is not statistically significant.
agent_relevance: Novelty judged on paper is a poor proxy. Test ideas by running them (G3).

source: Franceschelli and Musolesi (2024) Creative Beam Search
finding: Diverse beam search then model self-evaluation. Users preferred it modestly over plain sampling.
numbers: 217 answers: CBS preferred 45%, standard 29%, too similar 26%. Self-pick matched diverse-beam pick 29% vs 35.3% by chance.
limits: Small study, 7B chat model, 256 tokens. Judge is the model itself.
agent_relevance: Weak evidence that generate-and-test beats sampling; a quarter of outputs were not distinguishable.

source: Zhang et al. (2025) NoveltyBench
finding: 20 frontier models give far fewer distinct answers than humans; larger models in a family are often less diverse.
numbers: 10 samples at temperature 1: GPT-4o about 2.88 distinct of 10 on one panel; Llama-3.2-1B 6.74, Llama-3.1-8B 5.24, Llama-3.3-70B 2.49 (figure values, read from text extraction). Human baseline from 8 authors on 100 prompts.
limits: Humans were the paper authors, not a crowd. Distinctness is judged by a classifier.
agent_relevance: Bigger is not more varied. Matches CreativeBench.

source: Zhang et al. (2025) NoveltyBench
finding: Telling the model its earlier answers (in-context regeneration) restores diversity; asking for 'creative' output does not.
numbers: Regeneration lifted Claude-3 Opus, GPT-4o and Gemini 2.0 Pro to roughly human diversity; GPT-4o and Gemini 2.0 Pro exceeded human cumulative utility. Paraphrase and system prompt only marginal.
limits: Subset of 100 prompts, 8 generations.
agent_relevance: Direct support for a history-of-tried-ideas list in S3. Code should hold the list and feed it back.

source: Bellemare-Pepin et al. (2024) Divergent Creativity in Humans and LLMs
finding: On the Divergent Association Task GPT-4 beat the mean of 100,000 humans, but not the top human tail.
numbers: GPT-4 above human mean (significant); GeminiPro not different; GPT-4-turbo lower than GPT-4. High temperature (1.5) mean score 85.6, above 72% of humans. Repetition fell as temperature rose.
limits: DAT is a word-distance test, not a quality test. Newer model versions did not consistently improve.
agent_relevance: Temperature raises spread but not validated quality.

source: Jiang et al. (2025) Artificial Hivemind
finding: Different models give near-identical answers, so many models do not mean many ideas.
numbers: 26K open-ended queries, 70+ models. Cross-model mean pairwise similarity 71% to 82% (DeepSeek-V3 vs qwen-max 0.82, vs GPT-4o 0.81). Min-p decoding: 81% of pairs above 0.7 similarity, 61.2% above 0.8.
limits: Embedding similarity; sampling at top-p 0.9, T=1.
agent_relevance: Model ensembles share one space (G4). Diversity needs structure from outside the model.

source: Jiang et al. (2025) Artificial Hivemind
finding: Reward models and LLM judges are less calibrated to humans when raters disagree.
numbers: 31,250 human annotations, 25 raters per item. Calibration worse on idiosyncratic-preference items despite similar overall quality.
limits: Not all models tested.
agent_relevance: Model judging of novelty is least reliable exactly where it matters.

source: Novikov et al. (2025) AlphaEvolve
finding: Evolutionary search with an LLM mutator and automatic evaluator finds improved constructions. It rediscovers best-known results in most cases and beats them in some.
numbers: On over 50 open maths problems: matched best known on 75%, improved on 20%. Improved SOTA for 14 matrix multiplication targets; 48 multiplications for 4x4 complex matrices.
limits: Needs an automatic scorer. Gains grow with LLM quality.
agent_relevance: Search works when there is a code-checkable score. Without one, it does not carry over.

source: Novikov et al. (2025) AlphaEvolve
finding: Ablation: removing evolution, meta-prompt evolution or context from the loop lowers the result.
numbers: Figure 8 (tensor decomposition and kissing number tasks); I did not extract exact numbers.
limits: Two tasks only.
agent_relevance: Archive plus feedback loop matter, not only sampling.
